newsitem.title: USA: HFS to take charge for PHH acquisition.
newsitem.headline: HFS to take charge for PHH acquisition.

text.p: HFS Inc., a rapidly growing consumer services company, said Tuesday it will take a pre-tax charge of about $265 million in the second quarter for its pending acquisition of PHH Corp.
HFS announced in November a $1.7 billion stock deal to acquire PHH, a company based in Hunt Valley, Md., that provides vehicle leasing and maintenance, real estate and mortgage banking services.
HFS said it expects the charge to result in annual pre-tax cost savings of about $100 million, with the full benefit of the cost cuts beginning in 1998.
The company also said it will report first-quarter results with and without PHH, and that it expects results to exceed analysts' expectations in both cases.
"HFS has experienced very favourable operating trends in our existing businesses during the first 75 days of 1997," said Henry Silverman, chairman and chief executive of HFS.

"Existing home sales continue to accelerate and consumer confidence and travel spending continues to increase. Combined with our continued unit growth, we expect to announce our 18th consecutive quarter of record earnings."

HFS, based in Parsippany, N.J., franchises hotels and Century 21 real estate brokerage offices. It also owns Avis Inc., the world's second largest rental car system, and owns Resort Condominiums International Inc., the largest provider of vacation timeshare exchanges worldwide.
HFS's stock, which did not immediately begin trading when the New York Stock Exchange opened, added $1.25 to $66.375.
